name: Song marketing operations
prompt:
Run the existing Song marketing operations queue for Z:\My Songs, retaining due-only claims, batch limits, campaign gates and stop conditions.

Quiet blogworthiness record: before finishing, record Blogworthiness: PASS or FAIL with a short evidence-based reason and source evidence in the existing report or final handoff. For PASS also record the reader-interest angle, duplicate check and next action. Do not send or surface a standalone completion-check reminder.

Search exclusions and process ownership — 2 November 2026: Before local discovery, read the current 'Search narrowly and exclude generated storage' section in the shared AGENTS.md and honour the owning root's .rgignore. Start with known files and the exact source/document subtree. Exclude dependency stores, virtual environments, build/output trees, caches/test temp folders, models, generated media and unrelated worktrees; avoid blanket --hidden and drive/workspace-wide recursion. Put explicit exclusions after inclusion globs. Retain session_id/exit_code; poll a yielded search or cancel its actual owned process/tree and verify exit. Do not leave discovery running after moving on. Apply at the next safe step without restarting or interrupting existing productive work. Record the actual scope/exclusions used in the normal private run receipt; a saved rule alone is not adoption evidence.

[Hashtag discovery and use v1 — 24 October 2026]
When this job's authorised work involves keywords, campaign copy, social preparation or useful incidental evidence, follow Z:\My Songs\Workflows\hashtag-discovery-and-use.md and Z:\My Songs\Workflows\keywordmoves-evidence-research.md. Use KeywordMoves >=0.6.0 native evidence routes plus hashtag-planner discovery, exact-asset/platform fit/safety review and final-copy audit; keep natural queries, literal hashtags, native topics/tags and video tags distinct. Reject unrelated trends/reach bait; never pad sets or transfer demand across platforms. Merge plausible new song/tag/platform proposals and changed evidence through Z:\My Songs\skill-source\research-keyword-database\SKILL.md into the existing 21-column BOM Z:\My Songs\Keyword Targets\keyword-targets.csv with history preserved. Use each platform's treatment and fresh source dates/scope; inspect audit metadata.passed, actual caption/asset hashes and independently persisted native copy. Whole-post success is not per-tag attribution. Preserve original active dates, no-op/stop/read-only rules, leases, quotas, time/batch limits, costs, owner, approvals, schedules and notification policy. This adds no independent research sweep, paid/API/account action, post, public save, reschedule, new job or notification. Quiet jobs maintain only evidence actually encountered. Before completion record Blogworthiness: PASS or Blogworthiness: FAIL with reason/source evidence in the existing report/handoff; PASS retains angle, duplicate check and concrete next action/blocker. Saved guidance proves configuration, not adoption or improved reach.
[End hashtag discovery and use v1]

Scheduled-job browser access — Kieran, 28 October 2026: This scheduled job is explicitly authorised to use the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in in-app browser (`@Browser`) whenever it is useful for its existing authorised work. This supersedes any older prompt or AGENTS.md rule that disables or limits the in-app browser for this scheduled job. Prefer a sufficient connector/API/CLI when it is more reliable; browser access does not add authority for sends, publication, account changes, spending, rights commitments or sensitive disclosure. Reuse or open only the tabs needed, preserve other owners' tabs and unsaved work, close completed job-created or released borrowed tabs, and verify a fresh browser-tab inventory before handoff. If `@Browser` is unavailable in the scheduled run, record the precise capability hold; do not claim access or completion and do not switch to native whole-PC control.



Operate the combined song-marketing queue under Z:\My Songs\Reports\song-marketing-operations. This replaces separate song wakeups; it does not authorise a new campaign action or resume any paused campaign. Read Z:\My Songs\AGENTS.md, this folder's manifest.json, and guide.html first. Use the current Europe/London date.

Use C:\Python314\python.exe with operations.py in this folder. Run `due` for a read-only queue preview. If nothing is due, stop quietly without opening a browser, writing repetitive reports, generating media or waking another chat. Otherwise run `claim --owner <current CODEX_THREAD_ID>`. Retain the returned token and deadline. An existing lease is a hold: never delete it because of age. Verify its exact owning chat through supported chat status tools; only after proving that owner idle/stopped may `recover --token <token> --verified-owner-idle <exact-owner-id>` release it. Do not stop or interrupt an active owner.

Process only the selected profiles, sequentially, with no subagents or other-chat wakeups. Start at most three profiles and spend at most 45 minutes in the whole pass. Before each profile, verify the saved instructions SHA-256 against the manifest and read its full instructions.txt and profile.json. These retain the exact original campaign instructions, cadence, stop/end dates and source chat identity. Read the release's latest canonical state, local operator, previous checkpoint and same-date reports. Keep release-specific reports, visual language, lyric/timing authority, rights, route exclusions and provenance separate. Current project rules take precedence over older wording in a saved source prompt. A paused profile remains excluded until Kieran explicitly enables it.

Reuse current shared platform evidence across due songs where valid, retaining its observation date and limits. Do not reopen every artist dashboard for every song or launch a new render/model/scan simply to fill a run. Use the maintained DanceFlow workflows and complete capability review only for work that actually requires them. Kieran explicitly enabled in-app browser access for this Song marketing operations job on 23 October 2026. This is the named job-specific exception to the 19 October 2026 in-app-browser disablement in AGENTS.md, and applies to this saved job and the due campaign profiles it processes; other jobs retain their existing browser rules. Prefer supported connectors/APIs/CLI for suitable semantic operations; the in-app browser is permitted when interactive browser UI is needed. Read the current browser skill before use, reuse appropriate tabs, retain private ownership/evidence receipts, close completed job-created and released borrowed tabs through supported controls, and verify closure with a fresh inventory. Preserve active uploads, unsaved forms and other owners' work. Keep the existing lifecycle stop conditions: checkpoint and stop new in-app-browser work if any five-minute interval reaches 100 lifecycle/missing-frame events, missing-frame errors continue after navigation or teardown, or an idle/failed/interrupted chat retains browser ownership; do not enter retry loops. Use the authorised external Chrome extension or bounded isolated signed-out checks where appropriate. Do not kill/restart Codex, move state databases, or alter unrelated schedules or video renders.

All original permissions and current exact-action gates remain authoritative. Preserve the shared atomic duplicate-send gate, current Sent/submission recheck and exact payload approval before any external reply/submission. Apply the limited standing permission for eligible verified publicity only when every condition passes. Use the WordPress REST helper for source and public saves, metadata-derived timing, mobile-motion and rendered verification rules, and future social scheduling with YouTube/TikTok priority and same-job EPK reconciliation. Never infer an outcome from a receipt, draft or schedule.

Checkpoint every attempted profile with `record --token <token> --profile <id> --outcome completed|blocked|partial|no_action --evidence <actual-report-or-checkpoint-path> --note <brief-status>`. Completed means that due attempt is actually complete; record precise blocked/partial states otherwise. Partial work remains pending with a four-hour retry delay and fair queue ordering; do not label it complete. Maintain one coherent report per campaign and London date, preserving older dates. Do not start more work near the deadline; checkpoint and release instead. In a final cleanup step, run `release --token <token>` to record the batch and release ownership, even when some selected profiles were deferred. Retain unsaved forms/uploads with an exact hold and release completed browser work through supported controls.

Report only useful campaign results, required decisions, failures, or changed blockers. Keep coordination private and the result concise. Configuration, synthetic tests and successful queue selection are not evidence of campaign execution, public publication, physical-phone behavior or a fix for Codex crashes.
